correctness.rationale: The quotient condition \(x+y\in P\) yields the exact published component decomposition. If \(s=1\), the \(P\)-component is an isolated vertex. If \(s\ge2\), every complete or complete-bipartite component has total-domination number two, and every local minimum is an edge, so the same union is paired. Counting edges in each independent component gives \(\binom{s}{2}^{q}\) or \(\binom{s}{2}s^{q-1}\).

originality.rationale: Anderson and Badawi already give the complete component decomposition for a prime ideal: the ideal itself is an isolated complete component, while the remaining cosets are either disjoint complete graphs or inverse-paired complete bipartite graphs. Every formula in the package, including the minimum-set enumeration, then follows by multiplying the elementary two-vertex choices in those components. This is direct prior implication at the level of the whole graph.
